issues.detail: The Hebrew has three officials: תַּרְתָּן (Tartan), רַב סָרִיס (Rab-saris), and רַב שָׁקֵה (Rabshakeh). The Chinese renders 'תַּרְתָּן' as '長官' (a generic title) and 'רַב סָרִיס' as '拉伯撒利' (a transliteration), but 'רַב שָׁקֵה' is correctly '拉伯沙基'. The first name 'תַּרְתָּן' is not transliterated as a proper name (e.g., 他珥探) but replaced with a common noun '長官', which loses the specific personal name present in the Hebrew.

The Hebrew phrase 'מִן לָכִישׁ' (from Lachish) is rendered as '從拉吉城門' (from the gate of Lachish). The word '城門' (gate) is an addition not present in the Hebrew; the Hebrew only says 'from Lachish' without specifying 'gate'. This adds a detail not in the source text.
